content:
The image shows a plant leaf with a widespread, whitish-to-grayish coating on its surface. The coating appears granular or powdery in texture, covering a significant portion of the leaf. This directly matches the description of Powdery Mildew, which is characterized by white, powdery spots on leaves. The other options are less likely: Anthracnose typically presents as dark, sunken lesions; Die Back involves the death of twigs or stems starting from the tip; and Sooty Mould is a black, soot-like coating. The visual evidence strongly supports Powdery Mildew.
